why: The edit made NP-completeness part of the left-fragment severity, so the scorer reduced many cuts that split NPs (giving a small net gain). However, that change often achieved NP preservation by moving the preferred cut earlier (detaching tiny left fragments or cutting before an NP) which harmed a sizable set of mid-length examples; improvements are concentrated in the very short latency bins (≤3, ≤5) while ≤7/≤10 bins show small losses. Rank_depth falls at depth1 and rises at depth2, indicating the edit shifted the top choice rather than uniformly improving deeper rankings.
lesson: When increasing NP-completeness weight, preserve or improve top-1 alignment—avoid causing the model to favor earlier boundary placements that detach tiny left fragments even if they avoid cutting inside NPs.
